name: Paris
tagline: Light on the Seine, a table for every hour, elegance worn lightly.
whenBlurb: Come late May through June for long light, Roland-Garros and the couture calendar, or September into October for the art season; skip a shuttered, sweltering August and grey January.

ourTake.lede: Give Paris more mornings than you think you need, the Louvre before ten, the Marais before the shops open, a café before the city fills. The great mistake is treating it as a checklist of monuments; the real pleasure is a single arrondissement walked slowly, one long lunch, and the light going gold over the rooftops around seven. Skip the Champs-Élysées entirely and eat where the waiters don't speak English.
ourTake.comeIf: You want grand museums, three-star tables and quiet luxury within walking distance of each other.
ourTake.skipIf: You are chasing beaches, wilderness or an unhurried resort week doing nothing.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Le Bristol Paris
items.description: The grande dame of them all, a courtyard garden hidden behind the city's most powerful street.

items.name: Four Seasons Hotel George V
items.description: The Four Seasons standard our members already trust, wrapped in legendary flowers.

items.name: Le Meurice, Dorchester Collection
items.description: Starck's hand over an 18th-century bones, looking straight onto the gardens.

items.name: Hôtel Plaza Athénée, Dorchester Collection
items.description: The couture address, Dior at the door and the red awnings on the avenue.

items.name: Cheval Blanc Paris
items.area: 1st arr. / La Samaritaine, by the Seine
items.description: LVMH's newest icon, river light, a Dior spa, and a pool most hotels can only envy.

items.name: Hôtel de Crillon, A Rosewood Hotel
items.description: An 18th-century palace on the grandest square, restored without losing its nerve.

items.name: Le Royal Monceau – Raffles Paris
items.area: 8th arr. / near the Arc de Triomphe
items.description: The artist's palace, Starck design, its own gallery and cinema, a long quiet pool.

items.name: La Réserve Paris
items.area: 8th arr. / Avenue Gabriel, by the Élysée
items.description: A forty-key mansion that feels less like a hotel and more like a private house.

items.name: Shangri-La Paris
items.description: A Bonaparte prince's palace, with the Eiffel Tower filling many of the windows.

items.name: The Peninsula Paris
items.area: 16th arr. / near the Arc de Triomphe
items.description: Peninsula precision and a rooftop that trades on the finest view in Paris.

items.name: Bulgari Hotel Paris
items.description: Italian glamour dropped onto the smartest corner, with one of the city's largest hotel spas.

items.name: Hôtel Lutetia
items.description: The only Palace on the Left Bank, literary Saint-Germain in an Art Deco landmark.

items.name: Hôtel Fouquet's Paris, Barrière
items.description: Family-owned Barrière glamour above the most famous brasserie on the avenue.

items.name: The Ritz Paris
items.description: The most famous hotel name in the world, still keeping the promise on Place Vendôme.

items.name: Maison Villeroy
items.description: A discreet townhouse near the Élysée for members who prefer to be unseen.

items.name: Mandarin Oriental, Paris
items.description: A garden courtyard hidden off the smartest shopping street, run to the group's quiet precision.

items.name: Saint James Paris, Relais & Châteaux
items.area: 16th arr. / near the Bois de Boulogne
items.description: The only château-hotel in Paris, set behind its own gardens.

items.name: Park Hyatt Paris-Vendôme
items.description: Refined and understated, a calm base a step from the jewellers of Vendôme.

items.name: J.K. Place Paris
items.description: Italian-run, jewel-box luxury on the Left Bank, warm where the palaces can be grand.

items.name: Nolinski Paris, Evok Collection
items.description: A chic forty-five-key house between the Louvre and the Palais Royal.

items.name: Brach Paris, Evok Collection
items.description: Starck-designed and buzzing, with a rooftop garden and a fashionable crowd.

items.name: Grand Powers
items.description: Elegant, intimate and perfectly placed for a day among the maisons.

items.name: Le Burgundy Paris
items.description: Refined and central, with a spa and a Michelin-recognised kitchen of its own.

items.name: Château Voltaire
items.description: A fashion-crowd design hotel that hides its glamour behind a plain door.

items.name: Maison Proust
items.description: Belle Époque opulence and a La Mer spa, tucked into the Marais.

items.name: Le Grand Mazarin
items.description: Joyful maximalism and one of the liveliest hotel restaurants in town.

items.name: La Fantaisie
items.description: A garden-inspired newcomer with a rooftop and a light-hearted spirit.

items.name: Maison Delano Paris
items.description: Sleek and discreet, arranged around a quiet courtyard.

items.name: Le Pavillon de la Reine
items.description: Hidden behind the loveliest square in Paris, romantic and quiet.

items.name: Monsieur George
items.description: A warm, well-placed boutique with more soul than its size suggests.

items.name: Grand Hôtel du Palais Royal
items.area: 1st arr. / by the Palais Royal gardens
items.description: Elegant and superbly placed, a step from the arcades of the Palais Royal.

items.name: Relais Christine
items.description: A hushed Left Bank townhouse built around its own courtyard.

items.name: Eiffel Tower
credentials: most-visited paid monument in the world
items.description: The city's iron heart; go to the summit at dusk and catch the on-the-hour sparkle, or dine at the Jules Verne on the second floor for a table above Paris.

items.name: Arc de Triomphe
items.description: Climb the 284 steps to a rooftop where twelve avenues fan out like a star, with the Champs-Élysées running straight to the Louvre.

items.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
items.description: Reopened December 2024 after the 2019 fire, the restored nave gleams brighter than in living memory; entry is free, and the bell towers reopened in September 2025 for the climb to the gargoyles.

items.name: Sainte-Chapelle
credentials: finest medieval stained glass in the world
items.description: A jewel-box royal chapel where fifteen soaring windows of 13th-century stained glass wrap you in coloured light, go on a bright morning for the full effect.

items.name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
items.description: The white domed basilica crowns the highest point in Paris; the steps below give one of the great free panoramas, and the dome climb rewards with a 360° sweep.

items.name: Panthéon
items.description: A neoclassical temple where France buries its greats, Voltaire, Curie, Hugo, with Foucault's pendulum swinging under the dome and a colonnade viewpoint above.

items.name: Les Invalides & Napoleon's Tomb
items.description: Under the gilded dome lies Napoleon in six nested coffins; the complex also holds the Army Museum, strong on the family history-of-France angle.

items.name: Palais Garnier (Opéra)
credentials: inspiration for Phantom of the Opera
items.description: The most opulent theatre in Europe, grand staircase, gilded foyer, and a Chagall-painted ceiling; tour it by day or take an advisor-booked box for a ballet.

items.name: The Louvre
items.description: The world's largest art museum; ask us to arrange an early-access or after-hours private hour so you meet the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo without the crush.

items.name: Musée d'Orsay
credentials: Finest Impressionist collection in the world
items.description: A grand Beaux-Arts railway station turned temple of Impressionism, Monet, Renoir, Van Gogh, Degas, best from the giant golden clock window on the top floor.

items.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
items.description: Two oval rooms hold Monet's monumental Water Lilies, wrapping you in eight curved panels designed by the painter himself, a meditative, unhurried half-hour.

items.name: Musée Rodin
items.description: The sculptor's mansion and rose garden, where The Thinker and The Kiss sit among clipped hedges, one of the loveliest, calmest museums in the city, ideal with children.

items.name: Musée Picasso
items.description: A restored 17th-century mansion in the Marais holding the world's greatest Picasso collection, drawn from the artist's own estate.

items.name: Centre Pompidou
items.description: The inside-out building of coloured pipes houses Europe's biggest modern-art museum; note it is closing for a multi-year renovation, so confirm access with us before you plan.

items.name: Bourse de Commerce, Pinault Collection
items.description: François Pinault's contemporary art inside a domed former grain exchange reimagined by Tadao Ando, a concrete cylinder within a historic rotunda; the 2026 show 'Clair-obscur' runs into late August.

items.name: Musée Marmottan Monet
items.description: The world's largest Monet holding, including 'Impression, Sunrise', the painting that named the movement, in an intimate townhouse well off the tourist track.

items.name: Musée du Quai Branly, Jacques Chirac
items.description: Jean Nouvel's museum of the arts of Africa, Asia, Oceania and the Americas, wrapped in a living green wall, a thoughtful, less-obvious stop near the Eiffel Tower.

items.name: Petit Palais
items.description: The city's fine-arts museum in a jewel of a 1900 building, free entry, a gilded interior, and a serene garden café most visitors walk right past.

items.name: Grand Palais
items.description: Reopened in 2024 after a sweeping restoration, its vast glass-and-iron nave is Paris's grandest exhibition hall, check what blockbuster show is on.

items.name: Musée Nissim de Camondo
credentials: House museum of the Camondo family
items.description: A perfectly preserved aristocratic mansion of 18th-century French decorative arts, with a moving family history, a quiet gem beside Parc Monceau.

items.name: Musée Jacquemart-André
items.description: A collector couple's opulent townhouse hung with Italian and French masters; take tea in the frescoed dining room under a Tiepolo ceiling.

items.name: Le Marais
items.description: The best-preserved old quarter, Renaissance mansions, the arcaded Place des Vosges, designer boutiques and falafel lanes; wander with no plan, it rewards it.

items.name: Saint-Germain-des-Prés
items.description: Literary Left Bank of Café de Flore and Les Deux Magots, antique galleries and the city's oldest church, the neighbourhood for a slow morning and good browsing.

items.name: Montmartre
items.description: The village on the hill, cobbled lanes, the last working vineyard in Paris, artists in Place du Tertre, and hidden squares away from the crowds if you climb early.

items.name: Île Saint-Louis
items.description: A serene 17th-century island in the Seine, one main street of mansions and small shops, stroll the quays with a Berthillon ice cream, a Paris rite.

items.name: Canal Saint-Martin
items.description: Iron footbridges, plane trees and locks lined with young Paris; walk the canal to Bassin de la Villette, or take a slow boat cruise through the underground vaults.

items.name: Latin Quarter & Rue Mouffetard
items.description: Student Paris around the Sorbonne, plus the sloping market street of Rue Mouffetard, one of the oldest in the city, lined with cheese, wine and produce stalls.

items.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
items.description: The most beloved park in Paris, sail a toy boat on the fountain, watch a puppet show, and sit in the green chairs among statues and orchards; children adore it.

items.name: Jardin des Tuileries
items.description: The grand formal garden linking the Louvre to Place de la Concorde; ponds, statues and, in summer, a fairground with a big wheel over the treetops.

items.name: Palais-Royal Gardens
items.description: A hidden arcaded courtyard behind the Louvre, Buren's striped columns, lime-tree walks and old-world boutiques; one of the quietest lovely corners in the centre.

items.name: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont
items.description: The most dramatic park in Paris, cliffs, a lake, a temple on a crag and a suspension bridge; a local, family-filled escape far from the tourist centre.

items.name: Bois de Boulogne & Fondation Louis Vuitton
items.description: Paris's great western woodland for boating and gardens, now anchored by Frank Gehry's glass-sail Fondation Louis Vuitton, a landmark of art and architecture in itself.

items.name: Père Lachaise Cemetery
items.description: A hilly garden-necropolis of cobbled avenues and grand tombs, Chopin, Wilde, Piaf, Jim Morrison; strangely peaceful and beautiful, especially in autumn.

items.name: Galeries Lafayette Rooftop
items.description: Under the great stained-glass dome of the flagship store, then up to the free rooftop terrace for one of the best open-air views of the Opéra and Eiffel Tower.

items.name: Montparnasse Tower Observation Deck
credentials: Tallest observation deck in central Paris
items.description: The one skyline view that includes the Eiffel Tower, the 56th-floor deck and open rooftop give the finest sunset panorama in the city, minus the queues of the tower itself.

items.name: The Covered Passages
items.description: Glass-roofed 19th-century arcades, Galerie Vivienne, Passage des Panoramas, Passage Jouffroy, full of mosaic floors, old bookshops and tearooms; a rainy-day treasure hunt.

items.name: Marché d'Aligre
items.description: One of the liveliest, most authentic markets, a covered hall of fine cheese and produce plus an open-air flea market; go with us for a chef-led tasting stroll.

items.name: Rue Cler Market Street
items.description: A pretty pedestrian market street of cheesemongers, bakeries and florists near the Eiffel Tower, the classic spot to assemble a picnic for the Champ de Mars.

items.name: Marché aux Puces de Saint-Ouen
credentials: World's largest antiques and flea market
items.description: The world's largest antiques market, a sprawling maze of dealer stands in vintage furniture, art and curiosities; an advisor guide makes the labyrinth worthwhile.

items.name: Bouquinistes of the Seine
items.description: The green riverside book boxes are a UNESCO-listed Paris institution, browse antique prints, posters and old books along the quays between the bridges.

items.name: Seine Dinner Cruise
items.description: Glide past the floodlit monuments over a fine dinner; we book the private or premium boats, and can arrange a fully vegetarian or Jain-aware menu on board.

items.name: Avenue Montaigne
items.description: The couture spine of Paris, Dior, Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Valentino, flagship after flagship; we can arrange private in-store appointments and after-hours access.

items.name: Rue Saint-Honoré & Place Vendôme
items.description: From Colette concept-store cool to the high-jewellery houses of Place Vendôme, Cartier, Van Cleef, Boucheron, set around the Ritz; the address for jewels and watches.

items.name: Le Bon Marché
items.description: The world's first department store and still the most refined, with La Grande Épicerie next door for one of the great food halls in Paris.

items.name: Atelier des Lumières
items.description: A former foundry turned immersive digital art hall where masterpieces sweep across the walls and floor to music, a hit with children and the whole family.

items.name: Promenade Plantée (Coulée Verte)
items.description: The elevated garden walkway on a disused railway viaduct, the inspiration for New York's High Line, running above the arch-shops of the Viaduc des Arts.

items.name: Philharmonie de Paris
items.description: Jean Nouvel's silver concert hall with world-class acoustics; we secure seats for an evening of the Orchestre de Paris or a visiting name.

items.name: A Jazz Cave in Saint-Germain
items.description: Descend into a vaulted stone cellar like Caveau de la Huchette or Le Duc des Lombards for late live jazz, an intimate, only-in-Paris night out.

items.name: Perfume or Patisserie Atelier
items.description: Compose your own scent with a Grasse-trained perfumer, or spend a morning making macarons and éclairs with a pastry chef, a hands-on experience we tailor to the family.

items.name: Palace of Versailles
items.description: The supreme royal palace, Hall of Mirrors, the State Apartments, and vast formal gardens with the musical fountain shows; ask us for a private guide and skip-the-line timing.

items.name: Giverny, Monet's Garden
items.description: The painter's own water-lily pond, Japanese bridge and flower gardens, exactly as in the canvases, an unforgettable day trip in spring and summer bloom.

items.name: Château de Chantilly
items.description: A fairytale château in a moat, holding the finest old-master collection outside the Louvre, plus the Great Stables and a Le Nôtre park, quieter than Versailles.

items.name: Château de Fontainebleau
items.description: A royal residence for eight centuries, from Francis I to Napoleon, sumptuous, uncrowded, and set in a vast forest ideal for a family walk or ride.

items.name: Champagne Day Trip, Reims & Épernay
items.description: Cellar tours in the great houses along the Avenue de Champagne, chalk caves and tastings, plus Reims' Gothic coronation cathedral, a first-class day out we arrange end to end.

items.name: Kei
items.description: A Japanese hand on French cooking, exact to the millimetre, one of the city's nine three-stars.

items.name: Plénitude – Cheval Blanc Paris
items.area: 1st arr. / La Samaritaine, by the Seine
items.description: Sauces treated as the whole point, in a room that looks out over the river.

items.name: Arpège
items.description: The garden on the plate, Passard's near-vegan turn is the finest veg-friendly table at this height.

items.name: Le Cinq
items.description: Classical French haute in a palace dining room, the grand occasion, done properly.

items.name: Épicure – Le Bristol
items.description: French haute cuisine facing Le Bristol's garden, serene, precise, timeless.

items.name: Pierre Gagnaire
items.area: 8th arr. / Rue Balzac, near the Champs-Élysées
items.description: The avant-garde of modern French cooking, three stars held since 1996.

items.name: Le Gabriel – La Réserve Paris
items.description: Intimate three-star cooking inside one of the city's most private houses.

items.name: Alléno Paris au Pavillon Ledoyen
items.description: A pavilion in the Champs-Élysées gardens, and Alléno's modern French at full stretch.

items.name: Le Pré Catelan
items.description: A belle-époque pavilion set deep in the park, one of the loveliest tables in Paris.

items.name: Restaurant Guy Savoy – Monnaie de Paris
items.area: 6th arr. / on the Seine, the former Mint
items.description: The most-decorated name in the city by La Liste, in a riverside palace.

items.name: Table by Bruno Verjus
items.description: The international ticket of the moment, produce-led cooking from the counter.

items.name: L'Ambroisie
items.description: Old-guard grandeur on the most beautiful square in Paris.

items.name: Le Clarence
items.description: A private mansion, a Bordeaux cellar to match, and cooking of real depth.

items.name: La Scène
items.description: Stéphanie Le Quellec's precise modern French, one of the city's top kitchens.

items.name: David Toutain
items.description: Vegetable-forward modern French, curious and quietly brilliant.

items.name: Le Taillevent
items.description: A grande-maison institution, classical to its bones.

items.name: Le Grand Restaurant – Jean-François Piège
items.description: A jewel-box room and Piège's exacting modern French.

items.name: L'Orangerie – Four Seasons George V
items.description: The George V's lighter, luminous second table, no less serious for it.

items.name: L'Abysse au Pavillon Ledoyen
items.description: A sushi counter of rare finesse, within Alléno's pavilion.

items.name: L'Oiseau Blanc – The Peninsula Paris
items.description: French cooking on the rooftop, with the Eiffel Tower for company.

items.name: Le Jules Verne
items.description: Dinner inside the Eiffel Tower itself, the view every first visit wants.

items.name: Maison Rostang
items.description: Old-school luxury and classical French in Art Nouveau rooms.

items.name: Sushi Yoshinaga
items.description: An omakase counter working with fish of exceptional quality.

items.name: Alliance
items.area: 5th arr. / Left Bank, near the Seine
items.description: Restrained, precise modern French with none of the theatre.

items.name: Septime
items.description: The most coveted mid-price reservation in Paris, seasonal, confident, warm.

items.name: Frenchie
items.description: Greg Marchand's intimate, buzzing bistronomy, small room, big following.

items.name: Benoit
items.description: The only Michelin-starred bistro in Paris, Belle Époque, and run by Ducasse.

items.name: Allard
items.description: Escargots, sole meunière and a 1900s room, the Paris bistro, preserved.

items.name: Sharma Ji
items.description: The one genuinely Michelin-listed Indian in Paris, refined, and never a cliché.

items.name: Le Bon Georges
items.description: Produce and wine of unusual seriousness, in a warm neighbourhood room.

items.name: Desi Road
items.area: 6th arr. / Rue Dauphine, near Pont Neuf
items.description: A glamorous Indian bistro on the Left Bank with real vegetarian breadth.

items.name: Le Comptoir du Relais
items.description: The cult bistronomy address, a small counter that shaped a whole movement.

items.name: Chez L'Ami Jean
items.description: A lively Basque institution, generous cooking and a legendary riz au lait.

items.name: Le Baratin
items.description: The birthplace of bistronomy, still personal, still priced with restraint.

items.name: Pierre Sang in Oberkampf
items.description: Surprise tasting menus at an open kitchen, French technique, Korean soul.

items.name: Bistrot Paul Bert
items.description: The bistro of the imagination, steak-frites, soufflé, a wall of wine.

items.name: Clamato
items.description: Septime's seafood sibling, small plates, natural wine, no reservations.

items.name: Double Dragon
items.description: The Levha sisters' playful pan-Asian, bright, fun, generous.

items.name: Le Radis Beurre
items.description: Warm bistronomy and a blackboard menu, at a price that flatters the cooking.

items.name: Le Grand Bain
items.description: Creative small plates and natural wine in an easy, buzzy room.

items.name: Les Canailles
items.description: Simple French cooking done exactly right, the food a French grandmother would make.

items.name: Le Pantruche
items.description: A 1940s bistro mood and a short, seasonal menu that rarely misses.

items.name: Au Bon Accueil
items.description: Seasonal bistro cooking and a terrace that looks straight at the tower.

items.name: Mensae
items.description: French comfort cooking with real value, a neighbourhood room worth the trip.

items.name: Kokoro
items.description: A Franco-Japanese couple's regional French, touched lightly by Japan.

items.name: Chez Michel
items.description: A 1939 institution of Breton-leaning bistronomy, in a Japanese chef's careful hands.

items.name: Lao Siam
items.description: A flavour tour of Laos and Thailand, credentialed and unpretentious.

items.name: Impérial Choisy
items.description: Cantonese cooking done cleanly and well, in the heart of Paris's Chinatown.

items.name: Mandoobar
items.description: A tiny counter given over to Korean dumplings, made with real care.

items.name: Bar Hemingway, The Ritz Paris
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery
items.description: Twenty-five seats, a legend at the shaker, and the most storied cocktail room in Paris.

items.name: Bar Nouveau
items.description: The highest-ranked bar in Paris right now, Art Nouveau brought to life, drink by drink.

items.name: The Cambridge Public House
items.description: A British pub reimagined by serious bartenders, warm, unpretentious, world-class.

items.name: Danico
items.description: Velvet and gold in a covered arcade, precise cocktails behind Daniele Dalla Pola's counter.

items.name: Little Red Door
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, No. 6 (2023); 51–100 list (No. 59, 2024)
items.description: For a decade one of the world's most decorated bars, conceptual menus, faultless execution.

items.name: Candelaria
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, repeat listee (peak No. 9, 2013); Top 500 Bars 2025
items.description: The bar that began the Paris speakeasy era, a taqueria out front, a hidden room behind.

items.name: Le Syndicat
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, recent listee (No. 68, 2023)
items.description: French spirits only, Cognac, Calvados, Armagnac, behind a deliberately shabby door.

items.name: Cravan
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery; Difford's Guide top-50 bar
items.description: Franck Audoux's study of pre-1930s French cocktails, in a listed Art Nouveau corner house.

items.name: Combat
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery
items.description: A female-led room, light and green, from alumni of the Experimental Cocktail Club.

items.name: Le Tout-Paris, Cheval Blanc Paris
items.area: 1st arr. / La Samaritaine, by the Seine
credentials: Inside Cheval Blanc Paris (French Palace distinction)
items.description: The seventh-floor terrace of an LVMH palace, from Notre-Dame to the Eiffel Tower.

items.name: Les Ombres
items.description: A glass rooftop under Jean Nouvel's roof, with the Eiffel Tower almost close enough to touch.

plan.heading: 4 days in Paris, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Arrive at Le Bristol, then the Musée de l'Orangerie for Monet's Water Lilies in the round.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Tuileries and Place Vendôme on foot, a stop at the historic jewellers.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Le Cinq at the Four Seasons George V, three stars and impeccable service.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Louvre from opening, guided, keeping to the Italian galleries and the Egyptian wing.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Sainte-Chapelle for the glass, then a slow walk across Île Saint-Louis for Berthillon.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Guy Savoy on the Quai de Conti, overlooking the Seine.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Musée d'Orsay early for the Impressionists under the great clock.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Saint-Germain-des-Prés and the galleries of the Rue de Seine, coffee at Café de Flore.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Arpège, Alain Passard's vegetable garden on the plate.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A car to Versailles for a private morning in the State Apartments and the Hall of Mirrors.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The gardens and the Grand Trianon at a walk, returning by mid-afternoon.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final dinner at L'Ambroisie on Place des Vosges, classical and restrained.

items.name: Saint-Germain-des-Prés (6th)
items.description: Left Bank at its most literary and moneyed, for those who want galleries, old cafés and quiet luxury within walking distance.

items.name: Le Marais (3rd/4th)
items.description: Medieval lanes, the best small shops and a young energy, for repeat visitors who'd rather live in the city than tour it.

items.name: Rue Saint-Honoré / 1st
items.description: Palace hotels, the Louvre and the Tuileries at the doorstep, for a first visit where the icons should be close.

events.name: Roland-Garros (French Open)
events.note: The clay-court Grand Slam; the toughest ticket in Paris and worth timing a spring trip around.

events.name: Fête de la Musique
events.note: The whole city becomes a free stage on the solstice, every square and street corner has live music until late.

events.name: Nuit Blanche
events.note: An all-night contemporary-art takeover of the city, museums and monuments open through the small hours.

events.name: Fête des Vendanges de Montmartre
events.note: The Montmartre vineyard's harvest festival, parades, tastings and an old-Paris village mood above the city.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Base yourself in the 1st, 7th or 8th for the finest addresses; the best tables and couture appointments are booked well in advance, and a little effort with 'bonjour' before any request is always noticed.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Charles de Gaulle; a chauffeured car handles the 45-minute run into the centre, or a helicopter transfer to a heliport shortens it when time matters.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver for the city and day trips, though the Right Bank between the Louvre and the Champs-Elysees is a pleasure on foot.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Reliable throughout; an Orange or SFR eSIM is simplest, with fast wifi in hotels and most cafes.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Euro; cards are taken everywhere and cash is seldom necessary; service is included, so only a few euros are left for exceptional service.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: Late May-June and September offer warm, dry days and open terraces without August's heat. Avoid a shuttered, humid August when Parisians leave, and the wet chill of December-February.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Nonstop from Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru in about 9.5-10 hours. Air France (La Premiere and its refreshed business) and Air India serve it directly; Vistara-era product now under Air India. Air France's La Premiere ground service at CDG, with private car to the aircraft, is the finest connection touch on this route.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations beyond routine; safe, with normal vigilance for pickpocketing around tourist landmarks and the Metro. Tap water is safe to drink.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian dining is easy at the high end; strict Jain needs a quiet word ahead. Excellent Indian at Michelin-recognised places, and the Little Jaffna / La Chapelle quarter has authentic South Indian; ask the advisor to pre-brief kitchens on onion-garlic.
